name: ProPublica COMPAS Two-Year Recidivism
tagline: Audit criminal recidivism prediction, error-rate disparities, and leakage traps.
description:
Assembled via Florida public-records requests by ProPublica journalists Julia Angwin, Jeff Larson, Surya Mattu, and Lauren Kirchner (2016) from Broward County Sheriff's Office, Clerk of Courts, and Department of Corrections records (2013-2014), this 7,214-defendant dataset catalyzed the modern discipline of algorithmic fairness. ProPublica revealed that Northpointe's proprietary COMPAS risk score misclassified Black non-recidivists as Medium/High risk at nearly twice the rate of White non-recidivists (44.8% vs. 23.5%), whereas White recidivists were misclassified as Low risk far more often than Black recidivists (47.7% vs. 28.0%).

Technologically and pedagogically, raw COMPAS is the ultimate testbed for responsible tabular ML pipelines: out of 53 columns, 17 are PII strings, case numbers, dates, or SQLite join duplicates ('id', 'name', 'first', 'last', 'priors_count_dup') that freeze browser encoders if left checked, and 24 are proprietary COMPAS scores ('decile_score', 'score_text') or post-screening rearrest records ('is_recid', 'r_case_number', 'end', 'event') that cause catastrophic target leakage if not auto-disabled.

targetCandidates.description: Predict whether a defendant is rearrested within two years of COMPAS screening (1 = Rearrested, 0 = Not rearrested) using pre-screening criminal history and demographics.
Surrogate black-box audit: predict COMPAS's assigned risk tier ('Low', 'Medium', or 'High') from defendant demographics and prior counts to inspect how COMPAS weights race and age.

columns.name: id
columns.description: Internal ProPublica SQLite defendant record identifier.
columns.exclusionReason: Unique row identifier; causes overfitting and freezes one-hot encoders.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Defendant full name from public Broward County court records.
columns.exclusionReason: Direct personal identifier (PII) with 7,158 unique strings; must never be used in training.

columns.name: first
columns.description: Defendant given first name.
columns.exclusionReason: Direct personal identifier (PII) and demographic proxy with 2,800 unique strings.

columns.name: last
columns.description: Defendant surname.
columns.exclusionReason: Direct personal identifier (PII) and ethnic proxy with 3,950 unique strings.

columns.name: compas_screening_date
columns.description: Date on which the pretrial COMPAS risk assessment was administered.
columns.exclusionReason: Administrative timestamp string (690 unique dates); excluded to prevent UI-blocking high-cardinality encoding.

columns.name: sex
columns.description: Recorded binary sex of the defendant (80.6% Male, 19.4% Female).

columns.name: dob
columns.description: Defendant date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD).
columns.exclusionReason: Direct personal identifier (5,452 unique dates); age is already captured quantitatively in 'age'.

columns.name: age
columns.description: Defendant age in years at COMPAS screening.

columns.name: age_cat
columns.description: Discretized age tier used in ProPublica's fairness regression ('Less than 25', '25 - 45', 'Greater than 45').

columns.name: race
columns.description: Sheriff's Office racial/ethnic classification ('African-American', 'Caucasian', 'Hispanic', 'Asian', 'Native American', 'Other').

columns.name: juv_fel_count
columns.description: Number of prior juvenile felony offenses on record.

columns.name: decile_score
columns.description: Northpointe's proprietary 1-to-10 general recidivism risk decile output.
columns.exclusionReason: Proprietary COMPAS model output score; must be excluded when training an independent recidivism classifier.

columns.name: juv_misd_count
columns.description: Number of prior juvenile misdemeanor offenses on record.

columns.name: juv_other_count
columns.description: Number of prior non-felony/non-misdemeanor juvenile infractions.

columns.name: priors_count
columns.description: Total count of prior adult criminal offenses prior to COMPAS screening.

columns.name: days_b_screening_arrest
columns.description: Signed day offset between COMPAS screening and index arrest (ProPublica filtered to [-30, 30] in their 6,172-row subset).
columns.exclusionReason: Administrative record-linkage timing offset (307 missing values) rather than defendant risk attribute.

columns.name: c_jail_in
columns.description: Timestamp when defendant entered Broward County jail for the index offense.

columns.name: c_jail_out
columns.description: Timestamp when defendant exited Broward County jail for the index offense.

columns.name: c_case_number
columns.description: Broward County Clerk court docket number for the index charge.
columns.exclusionReason: Unique court docket identifier (7,192 unique values).

columns.name: c_offense_date
columns.description: Recorded date of the index alleged offense.
columns.exclusionReason: Administrative date string with 1,159 missing values.

columns.name: c_arrest_date
columns.description: Recorded arrest date when no offense date was filed (missing in 6,077 rows).

columns.name: c_days_from_compas
columns.displayName: Days From Index Offense to COMPAS
columns.description: Unsigned days elapsed between index offense/arrest and COMPAS screening.
columns.exclusionReason: Administrative record-matching interval unchecked by default.

columns.name: c_charge_degree
columns.description: Severity class of the current arrest charge ('F' = Felony, 'M' = Misdemeanor).

columns.name: c_charge_desc
columns.description: Free-text statutory description of the index charge (437 distinct strings).
columns.exclusionReason: High-cardinality statutory text (437 unique strings) that causes sparse one-hot bloat in browser models.

columns.name: is_recid
columns.description: Post-screening indicator of any subsequent rearrest regardless of the 2-year window.
columns.exclusionReason: Post-outcome recidivism indicator recorded after screening; directly leaks 'two_year_recid'.

columns.name: r_case_number
columns.description: Court docket number of the post-screening recidivism arrest (null if none).
columns.exclusionReason: Post-outcome rearrest docket number: non-null only when defendant reoffended.

columns.name: r_charge_degree
columns.description: Statutory severity of the subsequent rearrest offense.
columns.exclusionReason: Post-outcome rearrest attribute known only after recidivism occurs.

columns.name: r_days_from_arrest
columns.description: Days between recidivism arrest and booking.

columns.name: r_offense_date
columns.description: Date of subsequent rearrest offense.

columns.name: r_charge_desc
columns.description: Statutory description of the subsequent rearrest charge.

columns.name: r_jail_in
columns.description: Jail booking date for the subsequent rearrest.

columns.name: r_jail_out
columns.description: Jail release date for the subsequent rearrest.

columns.name: violent_recid
columns.description: Deprecated column left completely empty (100% null across all 7,214 rows) in ProPublica's export.
columns.exclusionReason: 100% empty legacy column in ProPublica's SQLite export (all 7,214 values missing).

columns.name: is_violent_recid
columns.description: Post-screening binary indicator of subsequent violent offense arrest.
columns.exclusionReason: Post-outcome violent rearrest indicator that directly implies general recidivism.

columns.name: vr_case_number
columns.description: Court docket number for post-screening violent offense.

columns.name: vr_charge_degree
columns.description: Severity tier of post-screening violent rearrest.

columns.name: vr_offense_date
columns.description: Date of post-screening violent offense.

columns.name: vr_charge_desc
columns.description: Statutory description of post-screening violent offense.

columns.name: type_of_assessment
columns.description: Constant string ('Risk of Recidivism') across all 7,214 rows.
columns.exclusionReason: Zero-variance constant metadata column ('Risk of Recidivism').

columns.name: decile_score_dup
columns.description: Duplicate of 'decile_score' produced by ProPublica's SQLite table join (disambiguated from duplicate header).

columns.name: score_text
columns.description: Coarsened COMPAS risk tier ('Low' = deciles 1-4, 'Medium' = 5-7, 'High' = 8-10); exhibits 44.8% FPR on Black non-recidivists vs. 23.5% on White non-recidivists.
columns.exclusionReason: Proprietary COMPAS categorical risk output (excluded when predicting 'two_year_recid', or usable as a surrogate-audit target).

columns.name: screening_date
columns.description: Duplicate screening date column from ProPublica's SQLite join.

columns.name: v_type_of_assessment
columns.description: Constant string ('Risk of Violence') across all 7,214 rows.
columns.exclusionReason: Zero-variance constant metadata column ('Risk of Violence').

columns.name: v_decile_score
columns.description: Northpointe's proprietary 1-to-10 violent recidivism risk decile.

columns.name: v_score_text
columns.description: Coarsened COMPAS violent risk category ('Low', 'Medium', 'High').

columns.name: v_screening_date
columns.description: Date of COMPAS violent risk screening.

columns.name: in_custody
columns.description: Custody start date used in ProPublica's Cox survival table.

columns.name: out_custody
columns.description: Custody release date used in ProPublica's Cox survival table.

columns.name: priors_count_dup
columns.description: Exact duplicate of 'priors_count' from ProPublica's SQLite join (disambiguated from duplicate header).

columns.name: start
columns.description: Start day of Cox proportional-hazards follow-up interval.

columns.name: end
columns.description: End day of follow-up (time until rearrest or 2016-04-01 censoring); directly reveals recidivism.
columns.exclusionReason: Post-outcome follow-up duration until rearrest or censoring; leaks 'two_year_recid'.

columns.name: event
columns.description: Cox survival event indicator closely tracking post-release rearrest.

columns.name: two_year_recid
columns.description: Whether the defendant was rearrested for a new offense within two years of COMPAS screening.

warnings: Construct Validity Warning (Bao et al., 2021): 'two_year_recid' measures rearrest rather than reoffending; differential policing intensity across Broward County neighborhoods conflates law-enforcement surveillance disparities with individual behavior.

Fairness Impossibility Theorem (Chouldechova, 2017; Kleinberg et al., 2017): Because observed rearrest base rates differ across groups (51.4% African-American vs. 39.4% Caucasian), no imperfect classifier can simultaneously satisfy Predictive Parity (calibration) and Equalized Odds (equal FPR and FNR).
Contains real public-record defendant names ('name', 'first', 'last', 'dob'); these PII columns are disabled by default and must never be used as model features.
